extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining prior art, obviousness, restriction requirements, and double patenting when copending applications, genus/species, combinations/subcombinations, or multiple species are involved in patent prosecution. Covers statutory tests (35 U.S.C. 102(e), 103(a), 121, 103(c)), procedural form paragraphs, and examiner burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copending application as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: A copending application with an earlier filing date that discloses the claimed invention (which has not been published under 35 U.S.C. 122) may constitute prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e); the copending application must have either a common assignee or at least one common inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate 102(e) form paragraph (e.g., 7.12) and consider overcoming evidence (37 CFR 1.132 derivation or 37 CFR 1.131 date-of-invention). If claims would have been obvious over the invention disclosed in the copending application, use provisional-obviousness form paragraph 7.21.01. If copending application conflicts with instant claims, also consider a provisional double patenting rejection (form paragraphs 8.30 and 8.32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date (AIPA vs pre-AIPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as amended by the American Inventors Protection Act (AIPA) and subsequent amendments to determine the copending application's prior art date unless the copending reference is based on an international application with an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000 (in which case pre-AIPA 102(e) applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply AIPA rules for references filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or national stages/WIPO publications of international applications with international filing dates on/after Nov 29, 2000 (form paragraph 7.12). Apply pre-AIPA 102(e) for U.S. patents issued from international applications filed prior to Nov 29, 2000 (form paragraph 7.12.01). See Examiner Notes for form paragraphs 7.12 and 7.12.01. Consider priority/benefit claims (119(e), 120, 121, 365(c)) only when subject matter is appropriately supported in the earlier application(s). Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) and 365(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: International publication exceptions to 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference is a publication of an international application that has an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000, did not designate the United States, or was not published in English by WIPO, it is not prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such references may instead be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of their publication date (see form paragraphs 7.08 and 7.09).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) based on copending application
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over a copending application that has a common assignee or at least one common inventor and an earlier effective U.S. filing date (presumption of future publication or patenting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection may be overcome by: (1) a 37 CFR 1.132 showing that any disclosed-but-unclaimed invention in the copending application was derived from the inventor of the instant application; (2) a 37 CFR 1.131 showing of an invention date prior to the copending application's effective U.S. filing date; or (3) showing the copending application is disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 103(c). Do not use this form paragraph when the copending application is disqualified under 103(c) for applications pending on or after Dec 10, 2004.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections based on other statutory categories (102(f)/(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: If evidence shows that either invention is prior art to the other under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) or (g), make a rejection using the appropriate form paragraphs (7.13 and/or 7.14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include such rejections in addition to any 102(e)/103(a) rejections when the factual record supports application of 102(f) or 102(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming 102(e)/103 rejections via derivation, inventorship, or terminal disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: A 102(e) or 103(a) rejection based on a copending or earlier-filed reference may be overcome by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 (derivation), 37 CFR 1.131 (earlier date of invention), or by an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 plus a terminal disclaimer per 37 CFR 1.321(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these procedural remedies where applicable; when claiming common ownership and prior inventorship, ensure compliance with rules for terminal disclaimers and 1.130 declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to give provisional double patenting rejection when claims conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claims of the copending application conflict with the claims of the instant application, a provisional double patenting rejection should be given (use form paragraphs 8.30 and 8.32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider statutory/nonstatutory double patenting and whether terminal disclaimers or other remedies apply; coordinate rejections with other applicable grounds (e.g., 102/103).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of improper joinder under 35 U.S.C. 121
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 121 provides that the validity of a patent shall not be questioned for failure of the Director to require the application to be restricted to one invention — i.e., no patent can be held void for improper joinder of inventions claimed therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When restriction is required by the Office, double patenting cannot be held if requirements of 35 U.S.C. 121 apply; ensure restriction practice is consistent with §121 and MPEP §1003.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for determining distinctness or independence
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Where inventions are independent (no disclosed relation), restriction to one is ordinarily proper. (B) Where inventions are related as disclosed but distinct as claimed, restriction may be proper. (C) Where inventions are related as disclosed but not distinct as claimed, restriction is never proper. (D) A reasonable number of species may be claimed when there is an allowable generic claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these general principles (see MPEP §806.06, §806.05, §806.04) when deciding restriction or double patenting issues; consult cited sections for specifics and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare claimed matter for distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: In questions of double patenting and restriction, it is the claimed subject matter that is considered and such claimed subject matter must be compared to determine distinctness or independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on disclosure; focus on claim scope. However, a provisional election of a single species may be required where generic claims recite so many species that an unduly extensive and burdensome search is necessary (see MPEP §803.02 and §808.01(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single embodiment claims defining same essential features
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claims of an application define the same essential characteristics of a single disclosed embodiment of an invention, restriction between such claims should never be required because the claims are different definitions of the same disclosed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such claims are voluntarily presented in different applications having at least one common inventor or assignee, consult MPEP §804-§804.02 for handling; do not treat as distinct inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus and species restriction criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application includes claims directed to different embodiments/species that could fall within the scope of a generic (genus) claim, restriction between the species may be proper if the species are independent or distinct. 37 CFR 1.141 provides that an allowable generic claim may link a reasonable number of species embraced thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application contains claims to more than a reasonable number of species, the examiner may require an election of species before taking further action. See MPEP §806.04 and 37 CFR 1.146 for election-of-species practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species may be independent or related — determine by disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Species are independent if they are not connected in design, operation, or effect under the disclosure. Where species are related under the disclosure, restriction practice must address both election-of-species rules and other restriction principles; restriction should not be required if improper under either practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include subcombinations usable with each other or intermediate/final product relationships — distinctness must be proven (e.g., no scope overlap, not obvious variants, and intermediate useful other than to make final product). See MPEP §806.04(b) and §806.05(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a generic claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic claim should require no material element additional to those required by the species claims, and each of the species claims must require all the limitations of the generic claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a generic claim is allowable, species claims that require all limitations of the generic claim will ordinarily be allowable over the prior art; if some species do not require all limitations, follow MPEP §821.04(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims limited to species (species claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim's scope may be limited to a single disclosed embodiment (a species claim); claims themselves are definitions or descriptions of inventions and thus are not 'species' in and of themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species always refer to different embodiments; determine whether species are independent or related as disclosed (see MPEP §806.04 and §806.04(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction between mutually exclusive species
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more species are claimed, a requirement for restriction to a single species may be proper if the species are mutually exclusive — i.e., claims do not overlap in scope (one claim recites limitations disclosed for a first species but not a second, and vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express mutual exclusivity as non-overlapping claim scope. If species overlap, restriction to one species is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species must be patentably distinct from each other
rubrics_metrics.description: In making a requirement for restriction among plural species, the examiner should group together species considered clearly unpatentable over each other and ensure species are patentably distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where generic claims are allowable, applicant may add species per 37 CFR 1.141. If species are voluntarily presented in different applications without an election requirement, investigate whether a double patenting rejection is appropriate (see MPEP §§804.01, 804.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic claim presented after issuance of species — double patenting risk
rubrics_metrics.description: If a generic claim is presented after issuance of a patent claiming one or more species within the scope of the generic claim, the Office may reject the generic claim on obviousness-type double patenting grounds when there is at least one common inventor/owner (or joint research agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may overcome such rejection by filing a terminal disclaimer. See cited Federal Circuit authorities (e.g., In re Goodman) and MPEP §804.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related inventions — principal distinctness test
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more related inventions are claimed, determine whether the inventions as claimed are distinct; if they are distinct, restriction may be proper; if not distinct, restriction is never proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For inventions in different statutory categories, generally only one-way distinctness is needed to support restriction; some relationships (e.g., combination/subcombination, related products/processes) may require two-way distinctness (see MPEP §806.05(c) and §806.05(j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination and subcombination distinctness criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To support restriction between combination and subcombination inventions, both two-way distinctness and reasons for insisting on restriction are necessary (e.g., there would be a serious search burden evidenced by separate classification or field of search). The inventions are distinct if: (A) the combination as claimed does not require the particulars of the subcombination as claimed for patentability, and (B) the subcombination can be shown to have utility either by itself or in another materially different combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the combination requires the details of the subcombination, inventions are not distinct and restriction must not be required. Use examples (ABsp/ABbr/Bsp diagrams) and form paragraphs (e.g., 8.15) when drafting restriction requirements. If combination claims are amended to require the subcombination particulars, maintainers should withdraw earlier restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural combinations and linking subcombination (linking claim) practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application includes a claim to a single subcombination that is required by plural claimed combinations, the subcombination claim is a linking claim and will be examined with the elected combination; plural combinations claiming a common subcombination are evidence that the subcombination has utility in more than one combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List linking subcombination in form paragraph 8.12; restriction between plural combinations may be made using form paragraph 8.14.01. If elected combination becomes allowable, reconsider restriction propriety and rejoin claims as required by MPEP §821.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcombinations usable together — restriction criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more claimed subcombinations disclosed as usable together in a single combination, and which can be shown to be separately usable, are usually restrictable when the subcombinations do not overlap in scope and are not obvious variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support restriction by demonstrating two-way distinctness and a serious search burden (e.g., separate classification). Presence of claims to multiple subcombinations can be evidence that the details of one are not required for patentability of a combination. Upon allowance of an elected combination or subcombination, the examiner must reconsider and rejoin allowable claims in accordance with MPEP §821.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on examiner to suggest separate utility
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden is on the examiner to suggest an example of separate utility for a subcombination or species when asserting distinctness; if applicant shows the suggested utility cannot be accomplished, the burden shifts to the examiner to document a viable alternative use or withdraw the restriction requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should provide concrete suggested utilities in the restriction action (see form paragraphs). Applicant rebuttal must be supported by facts; if convincing, examiner must either find an alternative separate utility or withdraw the restriction.
